target_customer: US consumers carrying credit card and other debt who want a plan to pay it down
problem: People with several debts lack a clear, automated payoff plan. ReadyForZero let users build plans, make payments, monitor credit and track progress online.
business_model: Freemium consumer fintech with premium upgrades and lender partnerships (about 4% of users upgraded, per TechCrunch 2015)

founders.name: Rod Ebrahimi
founders.background_notes: Education as shown on the YC company page.

founders.name: Ignacio Thayer
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2015 says he led engineering at Avant after the deal.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed secure account aggregation, payment flows and credit data integration, which are standard but compliance heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: User payoff plans and linked accounts add some stickiness, but personal finance tools were easy to copy and lender partnerships were the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in the sources found; Avant, an online lender, acquired it in March 2015 and the team joined Avant in Los Angeles.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2011) reports users eliminated about $42 million of debt within four months of beta launch, and LendingClub was a launch partner, indicating early demand.

branding.domain_note: Used readyforzero.com; the host did not resolve in this research session.

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the goal clearly and TechCrunch noted Avant kept it as an independent brand after the deal, but no mascot, community or brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: ReadyForZero raised a small seed in late 2010 and a $4.5M Series A led by Polaris in June 2011, reaching about a quarter million sign-ups by 2015 with roughly 4% on premium. Avant acquired it in March 2015 without disclosed terms and the team moved to Los Angeles. A Wikipedia summary says the platform was later shut down with no stated reason, so the YC Inactive status reflects absorption into Avant.
notes: Total raised: TechCrunch 2015 says about $5M, and the two TechCrunch 2011 rounds sum to about $4.76M. The $17K seed (2010-06) rests on a single database (SeedTable) and is probably the YC deal. Wikipedia says the deal closed February 2015 while TechCrunch dates the announcement 2015-03-31. Dealroom names Nagji Valade as a co-founder, which no company source confirms, so he is not listed. Competition list is empty: the dated competitor search returned only present-day aggregator lists. readyforzero.com did not resolve.
